To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the bottleneck for photoexcitation in Dirac materials is relieved by collective emission of multiple off-shell electron-hole pairs; 2) this emission results in a sharp angular distribution of the secondary carriers, resembling quantum-relativistic jets in high energy physics; 3) the off-shell cascade leads to efficient carrier multiplication, allowing emission of as many ∼10 secondary particles per single absorbed photon.
the photoexcitation of Dirac electrons is fundamentally different from the photoexcitation in conventional semiconductors.
the photoexcitation of Dirac materials is dominated by off-shell processes, resulting in quantum relativistic jets of secondary carriers.
